summary: Object: binds to one client-side object by id and exposes its properties reactively; the shared store behind repeater items and app state.
description: Object (Model2) is a window onto one object in the client-side object store. Bind it via `modelId` (or, per `idSource`, the enclosing repeater item) and the properties declared on the node become value outputs that update whenever anything writes the object — Set Object Properties, cloud-data nodes, scripts. `changed` fires on each such write. Objects are shared by id: every Object node with the same id sees the same data, which is how unconnected parts of a graph stay in sync.
whenToUse: Read client-side objects: repeater items, records fetched from the cloud (records are objects whose id is the record id), and structured app state. To write, pair with Set Object Properties or New Object; for lists use Array (Collection2); for scalar state use Variable.

ports.modelId: The object's id. Wiring a record id here binds to that record's client-side object.
ports.properties: The property list declared on the node; each name becomes a value output (and the editor's property inputs).
ports.changed: Signal; fires whenever any writer mutates this object.
ports.fetch: Signal; re-reads the object and re-emits outputs on demand.

runtimeBehavior: Property ports are generated from the `properties` list on the node instance (and the connected schema where one exists) — they are per-instance, not in the catalog. `idSource` swaps the id between an explicit input and the enclosing repeater item (declared-port-groups).
patterns: Repeater row: item id → Object → property outputs into the row's visuals.
Ids travel over wires; Objects resolve them where the data is needed.
antiPatterns: Duplicating object data into Variables 'for convenience' — bind another Object node to the same id instead; the store already shares it.
